newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee consumption stable in Jan-June 1996.
newsitem.headline: German coffee consumption stable in Jan-June 1996.

text.p: German coffee sales in the first half of 1996 were broadly steady compared with the same 1995 period, Frieder Rotzoll, managing director of the German coffee industry asssociation (DKV), said.

Rotzoll, who was addressing the F.O. Licht World Coffee Conference, said consumption in the full year was unlikely to continue the negative trend of 1995 and 1994, which brought respective sales declines of 2.5 and 3.7 percent.
"But I cannot be more specific at this stage," he said.
Green coffee equivalent sales of roasted and soluble coffee in 1995 were 564,000 tonnes (9.4 million bags) and per capita consumption fell to 6.9 kg from 7.1 kg in 1994.
Rotzoll said the high-prices of 1994 and 1995 had put off consumers, who also bought less coffee because of falling incomes and rising tax burdens.
Low retail prices this year were supportive, but the market would remain vulnerable to intense competition from other beverages.
The industry had made great strides forward with new products but needed to develop more new marketing channels.
